title: Recognition of a central isogeny from geometric fibres
statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative ring. Let $G$ and $H$ be reductive $A$-group schemes: smooth affine finitely presented group schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ whose geometric fibres are connected and have no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup, with group-scheme and reductivity conventions as in [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization], but without any splitness or torus hypothesis. Let $f:G\to H$ be a homomorphism. Assume that for every homomorphism $A\to\Omega$ to an algebraically closed field, $f_\Omega:G_\Omega\to H_\Omega$ is surjective and its scheme-theoretic kernel is finite over $\Omega$ and central in $G_\Omega$. Then $f$ is finite, flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], surjective and finitely presented, and its scheme-theoretic kernel $K$ is central in $G$. Here finite means affine with finite coordinate module over the target, and central means commuting with every group element after every algebra extension. Moreover $f$ represents the fppf quotient by $K$: the canonical map $G\times_AK\to G\times_HG$, $(x,k)\mapsto(x,xk)$, is an isomorphism and $G\to H$ is a cover for the topology of flat finitely presented surjective morphisms. No Noetherian hypothesis on $A$ or smoothness of $K$ is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.10 and its proof, printed pp.103--104; the discussion immediately preceding it supplies flatness, finite presentation and the fppf quotient description. This statement uses geometric fibres and does not assume global surjectivity separately. Read online; local PDF WANTED. No Stacks tag states this reductive-group theorem.

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $K=G\times_{H,e_H}S$. By [lem-a1-map-over-base-finite-presentation], $f$ is locally of finite presentation. A morphism between affine $S$-schemes is affine: over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ it is the morphism of spectra of its coordinate-algebra map. Consequently $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, hence finitely presented. Its base change $K\to S$ is also affine and finitely presented: if $A[H]\to A[G]$ is presented by finitely many generators and relations, tensor that presentation with $A$ via $e_H^*$.

source.place: Tag 02FV, lemma-finite-presentation-permanence; affine algebra presentation and base change.

proof.text: For an algebraically closed $A$-field $\Omega$, apply [lem-sfb-group-hom-dimension-kernel-image] to $f_\Omega$. Its closed image $I$ has the same underlying space as $H_\Omega$, since $f_\Omega$ is surjective. Thus $\dim I=\dim H_\Omega$, and the lemma gives $\dim G_\Omega=\dim H_\Omega+\dim K_\Omega$. Its criterion applies because $H_\Omega$ is smooth and connected, so $f_\Omega$ is flat. At an ordinary base point $s$, the projection $H_{\overline{\kappa(s)}}\to H_s$ is flat and surjective: on coordinates it is tensoring with a field extension. Each point lifts, and [lem-sfb-pointwise-flatness-base-change](2) descends flatness to $f_s$. Smoothness of $G\to S$ gives flatness by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. Now [lem-sfb-relative-flat-fibre-test] applies to $G\to H\to S$ (source flat and locally finitely presented; target locally of finite type), proving that $f$ is flat. It is surjective because every point of $H$ lifts to a geometric fibre, where $f_\Omega$ is surjective. By step 1, $f$ is therefore an fppf cover.

source.place: Discussion preceding Proposition 3.3.10, p.103; field flatness via the kernel-image dimension theorem; Stacks Tag 039E/039C fibrewise flatness criterion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relative-centre-multiplicative-base-change] to obtain $Z=Z_G$, of multiplicative type and compatible with every geometric base change. Apply [lem-sfb-multiplicative-source-kernel] to $f|_Z:Z\to H$. Its kernel $N$ is affine, flat and finitely presented over $S$, and the inclusion $N\to G$ factors through $K$; call the induced map $j:N\to K$. On every geometric fibre, the given scheme-theoretic centrality says $K_\Omega\subseteq Z_{G_\Omega}=Z_\Omega$. Therefore $N_\Omega=K_\Omega\cap Z_\Omega=K_\Omega$ as subgroup schemes, and $j_\Omega$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Theorem 3.3.4, pp.98--100, and Exercise 2.4.3, p.76; alternative assembly of the centrality argument in Proposition 3.3.10.

proof.text: The source $N$ of $j$ is flat and finitely presented over $S$ by step 3. Its target $K$ is finitely presented over $S$ by step 1. By [lem-a1-map-over-base-finite-presentation], $j$ is locally of finite presentation. All the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-flat-geometric-fibre-open-criterion] are now satisfied, and $j_\Omega$ is an isomorphism for every geometric point by step 3. Thus $j$ is an isomorphism. The inclusion $K\hookrightarrow G$ consequently factors through $Z_G$; this proves centrality after every algebra extension, not only on field-valued points. It also identifies $K$ as a group of multiplicative type of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 039E, lemma-morphism-between-flat, geometric-fibre isomorphism consequence recorded in the cited node; Conrad Lemma B.3.1, p.288.

proof.text: Fppf-locally on $S$, step 4 identifies $K$ with $D(M)$ for a finitely generated abelian group $M$. Every nonempty chart has a geometric point, and its fibre $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega[M]$ is finite by hypothesis. Since $\Omega[M]$ has basis $(e_m)_{m\in M}$, this forces $M$ to be finite. On this chart $\mathcal O[M]$ is therefore finite free with that same basis, so $K$ is finite there. These fppf charts form an fpqc covering by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]; [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-finite] proves that $K\to S$ is finite. This uses no smoothness of $K$ and allows torsion in $M$ divisible by residue characteristics.

source.place: Tag 02LA, lemma-descending-property-finite; explicit group-algebra basis calculation.

proof.text: For any $S$-scheme $T$, if $f(x)=f(y)$ for $x,y\in G(T)$ then $x^{-1}y\in K(T)$. Thus $(x,k)\mapsto(x,xk)$ and $(x,y)\mapsto(x,x^{-1}y)$ are inverse natural transformations between $(G\times_SK)(T)$ and $(G\times_HG)(T)$. They are morphisms formed from multiplication and inverse and satisfy the displayed identities as scheme morphisms. Hence they give the asserted isomorphism. Since $f$ is an fppf cover, any $T\to H$ lifts over the fppf cover $G\times_HT\to T$; two lifts differ uniquely by $K$ through this isomorphism. Sheafifying the pointwise quotient therefore gives $H$, with quotient map $f$. To justify the sheaf assertion, [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc] makes every fppf covering an fpqc covering, and [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] makes maps to $H$ a sheaf: compatible local morphisms descend uniquely. The quotient map is sectionwise injective by the displayed kernel calculation and locally surjective by the cover, so its associated sheaf is this representable sheaf.

source.place: Tag 023Q, lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms; explicit group torsor calculation as in Conrad Exercise 3.4.6(i), p.105.

proof.text: Under the isomorphism of step 6, the pullback of $f$ along itself is $G\times_SK\to G$. It is finite: tensoring a finite set of $A$-module generators of $A[K]$ with $A[G]$ gives finite $A[G]$-module generators of $A[G]\otimes_A A[K]$. The singleton cover $f:G\to H$ is fpqc, since it is flat and surjective by step 2 and affine, hence quasi-compact, by step 1. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-finite] to this cover to conclude that $f$ is finite. Together with steps 1, 2, 4 and 6 this gives all the claimed assertions.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q128-83d6fd87e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: The statement is unchanged from base dagsnap 8192019e; on the base the item was unsplit with no proof, so this is a first split and the re-split rule does not apply. All 7 steps were checked against the cited statements. (1) a1-map-over-base-fp gives f lfp; f is affine, hence fp; K is fp by base-changing the presentation. (2) The group-hom dimension lemma: a surjective f_Omega makes the image I have the same underlying space as H_Omega; H_Omega is smooth and connected, so f_Omega is faithfully flat. Clause (2) of pointwise-flatness-base-change descends flatness along H_Omega->H_s, with G_s x_{H_s} H_Omega = G_Omega. lem-pc-smooth-flat and relative-flat-fibre-test then make f flat, and surjectivity comes from the geometric fibres. (3) Centre node gives Z_G; kernel node applies to f|_Z (Z multiplicative type fp, H affine fp); the scheme-theoretic centrality hypothesis plus base change of Z gives N_Omega = K_Omega. (4) flat-geometric-fibre-open-criterion with N flat lfp, K fp and j lfp gives N = K, so K is central and of multiplicative type. (5) On each nonempty chart Omega[M] finite forces M finite; fppf->fpqc comparison and Stacks 02LA give K finite. (6) The torsor iso is explicit; sheaf property via fpqc representable descent. (7) The pullback of f along f is G x K -> G, which is finite; descend along the singleton fpqc cover {f}. New nodes are true (tested GL_n, SL_n with mu_n non-smooth, PGL_n; power maps, weight maps, trivial map with infinite kernel). Neither is in the DAG: the existing centre nodes are Noetherian-base, field or split only, and the existing kernel nodes cover split targets, monomorphisms or Noetherian local bases. Neither restates an item clause. Stacks tags 02FV, 039E, 039C, 02LA and 023Q were verified by label. Conrad's notes are online-only and recorded as WANTED, matching the item's inherited source. The four declared off-unit tool uses (map-over-base fp, fpqc descend finite, fppf-is-fpqc, fpqc representable descent) are generic and accepted.
